claims.statement: `CONTEXT.md` at the repository root is this project's canonical domain glossary: a Chinese single-context document whose 28 live entries pair a bold headword with a definition and an explicit `_Avoid_` list of rejected synonyms, and whose tail section `## 已退役词汇` registers twelve retired headwords with retirement dates and reasons. The README points at it as authoritative including that section, and `AGENTS.md` records the single-context layout as root `CONTEXT.md` plus `docs/adr/`.

`docs/agents/domain.md` makes the glossary normative for downstream work: agents read `CONTEXT.md` and the ADRs touching their area before exploring, name domain concepts with the glossary term instead of a synonym the glossary avoids, treat a missing term as a signal to reconsider the wording or record a gap, and surface a contradiction with an existing ADR explicitly rather than overriding it silently.

The session-activity vocabulary has a single definition: `RUNNING_WINDOW = 90.0` and `ACTIVE_WINDOW = 600.0` are declared once in `app/src/main/scanners/types.ts` and imported by every scanner, the shared record builder defaults `running` to `age <= RUNNING_WINDOW`, and both constants are re-exported from `scanners/index.ts` so no caller restates 90 s or 600 s.

The five AI tools share one four-state vocabulary (`RUN`/`CONFIRM`/`DONE`/`IDLE`) but derive it per scanner: only qoder can produce `CONFIRM`, because it requires the session's own event stream to end in an unanswered `tool_use`; hermes produces `RUN` from an active-session lease or an unended session and otherwise `IDLE`/`DONE`; zcode and kimi code produce only `RUN`/`DONE`; kimi work adds `DONE`/`IDLE` from its status map. ADR-0003 records that asymmetry as an accepted distortion of the unified model.

The tool-label vocabulary is carried by the session record's `tool` field, whose five values (`qoder`, `hermes`, `zcode`, `kimicode`, `kimiwork`) are the keys of `SCANNERS` and of `defaultSessionRoots`; the two-letter row marks (QD/KC/KW/ZC/HM) are rendered inside this repository by the sessions card, which falls back to `??` for an unknown tool.
Session identity is the pair `tool` + `id` rather than the tool-local id alone, because session ids from different tools can collide and would otherwise overwrite each other in the renderer.

Classification is a rule-based baseline rather than the final verdict: `zoneOf` maps shortcuts and `.url` files to `app` and files and folders to `doc`, and the desktop service then rewrites `zone` for every name listed in the layout store's `dock`/`docs` lists before planning, so a cross-zone drag changes which segment an item competes in. The retired `recycle` and `untouched` zone values have no successor and the panel carries no recycle bin.

The app zone's order is the concatenation of three segments: `pinned` (pin-list order, filtered to names present in the pool, de-duplicated with first mention winning), then `placed` (store order minus pins), then `recommended` (the remaining items sorted by descending usage score with name ascending as the tiebreak, an unscored item eligible at score 0); the plan exposes each entry as `{name, source}` with `source ∈ {pinned, placed, recommended}`, which makes 'a recommendation never displaces a hand-pin' structural rather than a sorting accident.

The hand-pin list is the `pinned` array of the machine-written layout store `userData/layout.json`, not a repository-root file, and no UI writes it: the desktop service loads it once at construction, planning filters it to names present in the item pool while stale names are kept so a returning file finds its place, the whole store is rewritten on every placement change, and the settings overlay offers only the factory reset — so hand-editing takes effect at the next start and is overwritten by the next placement change.

The doc zone is laid out by six extension-derived groups under a fixed `GROUP_ORDER` (`folders`, `office`, `pdf`, `image`, `archive`, `other`) — folders matched by kind first, then the office/pdf/image/archive extension sets, with `other` as the only fallback — and each group's members are assembled as the explicitly placed members in store order followed by everything else sorted by descending `mtimeMs` with name ascending as the tiebreak.

Because ADR-0002 confines the usage log to process path plus timestamp, the frequency score cannot rank documents: the doc zone orders items by file modification time, and the usage score is used only to order the dock's recommendation segment.

Usage frequency is defined as true start counts — a process going from absent to present, detected by diffing pid sets so that a second instance of the same path or a restart still counts — weighted by exponential decay with `HALF_LIFE_DAYS = 14.0`; the scoring functions are pure with the current time injected as a parameter, and only `start` events feed the score while `focus` events are recorded but never scored.

The usage log writes per-day JSONL files prefixed `start-` and `focus-` whose records contain exactly `ts` and `exe`, retains `RETENTION_DAYS = 90`, is collected at a 2-second cadence (`DEFAULT_USAGE_MS`) by the usage service inside the data-plane utilityProcess child, and is pruned of expired day files at boot and then hourly rather than by the panel's 1 Hz bridge tick.

The no-window-title rule is enforced by standing TypeScript tests: one asserts that the file the collector actually writes contains exactly `{ts, exe}` at the append level, and a repo-wide guard fails if any `*.ts` under `src/main` contains `GetWindowText` or `window_title`.

The cold-start prior is read only from the `UserAssist` registry key — `reg.exe export` of the `\Count` subkeous branches, ROT13-decoded value names, with the run count and FILETIME at fixed binary offsets and non-`.exe`/`.lnk` entries dropped — and is fused with the self-written log at the desktop-item level with weight `1/(1 + log start count for that item)`, so an empty log still yields a non-empty ranking while the prior retires as the log accumulates.

Drift correction is retired and must not be revived as an 'auto-arrange' feature: the panel draws desktop items itself, so there is no icon position for a system process to disturb, and the durable record of user intent is an order of display names (the `dock`/`docs` lists) rather than a map of coordinates.

The desktop watcher is a promptness device, not a source of truth: it watches both desktop roots, merges an event storm into one callback after a settle window (300 ms default), does not distinguish create from delete from modify the way the retired name-set watcher did, exits silently when a root cannot be watched, and leaves the 1 Hz scan round as the reconciling fallback — a failed scan keeps the previous round's items instead of emptying the dock.

Arrangement has one mode today: every scan round re-derives the whole plan from the item pool, the layout store and the usage scores, driven by the 1 Hz bridge tick and by the settle-debounced directory watcher; the retired model's one-shot dry-run/`--apply` arrangement command, its read-back coordinate verification and its 'single-item incremental' mode have no successor.

Layout snapshots are retired and replaced by the layout store plus one reset action: `userData/layout.json` holds the three ordered name lists that are the whole persistence of desktop carry state, `desktop/reset-layout` clears the explicit placements while keeping the hand-pin list, and there is no coordinate map, no factory-vs-run snapshot pair and no restore-to-snapshot path anywhere in the current code.

The desktop carry path never moves, renames or deletes a desktop file: planning emits an ordering only, the renderer draws the items, launching goes through the shell after a pool membership check, and the changes this application makes outside its own data are explorer's desktop-icon visibility toggle and the Startup shortcut.

The search panel's vocabulary is three UI states over a two-state machine: `SearchUiState` is `'idle' | 'active' | 'offline'`, the service's machine holds `idle`/`active` with `offline` derived and only while active, activation is idempotent, deactivation clears the query, voids in-flight responses and resets backoff and the offline badge; because the panel window is created unfocusable, activation additionally enables the host's temporary keyboard mode and deactivation disables it.

`classifyFailure` separates three failure vocabularies: `offline` only for a connection failure or a `SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE` payload, `rate_limited` for `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`, and `error` for a reachable engine returning malformed or unknown responses. The panel renders `ENGINE OFFLINE` and retries every 3 seconds when offline, backs off silently and re-sends the same query when rate limited (0.5 s doubling, capped at 5 s), and neither shows offline nor auto-retries on `error`.

Search query text never reaches the project's own artifacts: the renderer's evidence events carry only a query length (`qlen`), a behaviour test runs a whole search flow and asserts the probe word appears in no file under the usage directory, and a source test forbids `search/engine.ts`, `search/client.ts` and `services/search.ts` from importing the usage log, writing files, or containing a hard-coded HTTP URL — the engine host is the constant `127.0.0.1` with the port from `config.search`.

The glossary's retired register names twelve headwords with dates and reasons in three families: the service stack (data service, watchdog, search overlay window — retired 2026-09-29 with ticket 11), the desktop-layout mechanisms (drift correction and layout snapshot, retired 2026-09-25), and the wallpaper-visual vocabulary (Qoder status block, mouse indicator, head parallax, information module, HUD mode, cockpit wrap, instrument tilt). The HUD family is gone entirely rather than reduced to static perspective, and the wallpaper assets that carried those transforms are frozen read-only rather than maintained.

ADR-0001 is superseded by ADR-0004 and its zone vocabulary is inverted: zones are no longer a convention over real icon coordinates arranged through `LVM_SETITEMPOSITION`, but panel-drawn regions carrying panel-drawn items, so the write-endpoint and layout-snapshot consequences that followed from ADR-0001 are void and the only changes this application still makes outside its own data are explorer's icon-visibility toggle and the Startup shortcut.

ADR-0002 still governs the telemetry vocabulary: window titles are excluded at the collection path rather than filtered on the way out, and its accepted consequences are that frequency means start counts rather than foreground time, that documents cannot be ranked by frequency, and that a process path reaches a desktop icon by resolving `.lnk` targets — with unmappable processes still logged but excluded from the ranking.

The multi-tool ADR governs the session vocabulary: each tool keeps its unchanged upstream format read by one strictly read-only scanner rather than being migrated to a shared intermediate store, and a tool whose source is missing, locked or corrupt is skipped silently with a log line so panel availability wins over fault visibility. SQLite is opened with `readOnly: true` and a short busy timeout so a locked database fails fast instead of stalling the scan round.

The search-panel ADR is superseded by ADR-0004: because the panel can now receive clicks and keyboard inside its hotzones, search lives inside the panel as an HTML overlay instead of a separate service-owned Tk window, and the Listary query goes from the kernel service to the engine's loopback HTTP API — never from the renderer, which is why the API's missing CORS support stays irrelevant.

Two ADR files are both numbered `0003` — `0003-multi-tool-unified-session-model.md` (accepted) and `0003-search-panel-service-window.md` (superseded by ADR-0004) — and `0001` is likewise superseded by `0004`, so ADRs must be cited by filename rather than by number alone, with the README's ADR table as the record of each file's status.

The glossary rejects specific synonyms per headword (`后端`/`server` for 数据服务, `widget` for 信息模块, `fence` for 桌面分区, `launcher` for 搜索面板, `pin` for 手钉), and the avoidance rule applies to prose and issue text only, not to identifiers: the code keeps `pinned`, `dock` and `docs` in the layout store because there is no cleaner English identifier.

Clicking a session row sends only the tool name: the renderer invokes `session/focus` with the tool and never invents a path, the response is the three-way `FocusAction` (`focused` | `launched` | `degraded`), and the decision kernel resolves window or launch target solely from `config.tools`, degrading silently for an unknown or mis-shaped tool mapping.

There is no dock capacity limit: `planDock` takes no slot count and emits one entry per app-zone item, and a long dock is absorbed visually by a `flex-wrap` strip bounded by `config.desktop.dockMaxWidth`, so the glossary's 栏位 (slot) description as a fixed-coordinate cell with a capped total — including its 'when the slots are pinned full, recommendations do not appear' clause — is historical, and what survives of the word is position plus source.

The layout store is the only persistence of desktop carry state and holds three ordered display-name lists (`pinned`, `dock`, `docs`) with no coordinates at all: a missing or corrupt store self-heals to the factory state of empty lists, an explicit placement is recorded as 'before which item', the store is written by the desktop service alone, and the factory reset clears `dock`/`docs` while keeping `pinned`.

Doc-zone columns are computed by one zone-global cursor: an empty group consumes no column, a group occupies `ceil(count / docMaxRows)` contiguous columns, each non-empty group is followed by exactly one spacer column, and a ninth item folds into the column immediately right of the first eight; the single `config.desktop.docMaxRows` value feeds both the planner and the CSS grid, and an overfull zone is clipped visually by `docZone.maxWidth` rather than dropped from the plan.

The Python-era usage log at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\qoder-deck\usage` is migrated once into `userData/usage` on first run: day files inside the retention window are copied while the old directory is left in place, non-day files and files already past retention are skipped, and the migration is idempotent per file with line-level de-duplication so an interrupted run neither loses history nor doubles a record.

The independent panel is a transparent, frameless, never-focusable window created with `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true)`; pass-through is lifted by a 25 ms cursor poll against renderer-declared hotzone rectangles, a leave is confirmed only after two consecutive misses, pass-through is restored without the `forward` option because `forward` would make Electron install a system-wide low-level mouse hook (ADR-0005's red line), and leaving a hotzone re-pins the window to the bottom with a 500 ms throttle.

A desktop component is a plugin directory containing `plugin.json` (`id`, `name`, `version`, `entry`, `capabilities`, optional `mount`/`order`); `id` doubles as the `deck-plugin://<id>/…` protocol host and is restricted to a lowercase hostname character set, `entry` must be a `.js`/`.mjs` path inside the plugin's own directory (absolute paths, drive letters and `..` rejected), and asset reads happen only in the main process — the sandboxed renderer receives URLs, never file handles.

A plugin capability name is a snapshot section name and the cropping direction is 'give less, never more': a plugin receives only the sections it declared, unknown capability strings are discarded without invalidating the manifest, and the renderer builds the plugin view by looking up each declared capability in the snapshot.

Desktop components are hot-pluggable without a restart: the host scans its roots at construction and on `fs.watch` events, loads, disposes and reloads through the cordis lifecycle, bumps a per-asset revision so a reloaded entry URL bypasses the ESM module cache, lists a broken plugin with `status: 'error'` for silent panel-side degradation, pushes `plugins/changed` independently of the 1 Hz snapshot, and scans the built-in roots first so a same-`id` user plugin cannot displace a built-in component.

The built-in desktop components are the four card plugins under `app/src/renderer/cards/` (clock, hardware, sessions, weather) plus the calendar that stays in the host page; the README line and an `index.ts` comment that say five built-in components are stale, and the retired `qoder` segment is absent from the capability list.

The autostart item is one `AGENT DECK.lnk` in the current user's Startup folder and is a machine-level deployment record rather than a per-run install record: only a run whose application directory equals the declared `config.autostart.appDir` may create it or adopt a dead link, an existing link pointing at a live target elsewhere is never chased, a legacy `qoder-deck-server-watchdog.lnk` is deleted unconditionally on every start, and `enabled: false` removes the link.

Each retired headword has a named successor in the current design, which is what makes the retired register readable rather than a list of holes: data service → the cordis kernel services plus the data-plane child; watchdog → the outer supervisor with its detached restore watcher; search overlay window → the in-panel search panel; drift correction → panel-drawn items with an explicit placement order; layout snapshot → the restore-factory-layout action alone; Qoder status block → the session list card; information module → the desktop component.

The glossary's 'no border, no background' rule for 桌面分区 now holds for one zone only: the document zone is an unfilled container marked by the single `DOCS` zone label, while the application zone is drawn as a filled, bordered, rounded dock strip, and the zone-label vocabulary has no application-zone counterpart.

The dock's middle source has no glossary headword: `DesktopDockSource` is `'pinned' | 'placed' | 'recommended'`, but the glossary names only 手钉 and 推荐位, leaving the user's explicit drag placement (`placed`) unnamed even though it is the only ordering a user can express through the panel UI besides the pin list, and it is recorded as the `dock`/`docs` order lists.

`app/config.json` is the user-editable copy of production values and its sections map one-to-one onto the vocabulary: `panel` for the independent panel's geometry, `desktop` for the zone geometry and fold height, `search` for the Listary port, `appearance` for card opacity, `tools` for session-row launch targets, `plugins` for the desktop-component installation directory and `autostart` for the Startup link. Invalid fields fall back to defaults with a warning instead of being silently swallowed, an unparseable file is left untouched, and the whole file is rewritten atomically because settings changes persist through it.
